new_entities.name: Sacubitril-valsartan for HFrEF
aliases: ARNI therapy in reduced-EF heart failure
sacubitril/valsartan in chronic systolic heart failure
new_entities.description: Use of the angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor sacubitril-valsartan in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.

edges.effect_quant: PARADIGM-HF showed lower all-cause mortality with sacubitril-valsartan than with enalapril (HR 0.84), and a later clinical-trials meta-analysis reported fewer disease-related events overall (OR 0.82).
edges.population: adults with chronic symptomatic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction receiving guideline-directed medical therapy
edges.mechanism: Combined neprilysin inhibition and angiotensin receptor blockade improves neurohormonal control beyond ACE inhibition alone, reducing progressive pump failure and cardiovascular death.
edges.summary: Sacubitril-valsartan is one of the central mortality-improving therapies in modern HFrEF care. The strongest evidence comes from direct randomized comparison against enalapril rather than from weaker observational datasets.
edges.caveats: Benefits are clearest in ambulatory chronic HFrEF populations similar to PARADIGM-HF and come with more hypotension. The edge is about mortality benefit, not necessarily equal tolerability or applicability in every advanced or unstable patient.

evidence.citation: McMurray JJV et al 2014 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Angiotensin-neprilysin inhibition versus enalapril in heart failure.

effect_quant.comparator: all-cause mortality in PARADIGM-HF with sacubitril-valsartan versus enalapril
